issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named create_zero_state(num_qubits) for the tensor-network exercises, but the template repository defines the zero-state initializer as init_zero_state(num_qubits). This name mismatch is structural: students following the problem text will look for create_zero_state in the template, and tests or instructor-provided solution code may call create_zero_state. The inconsistency can block students or cause confusion about which symbol to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function init_zero_state to create_zero_state (keeping the same signature), or add a thin wrapper create_zero_state that calls init_zero_state. Also update the template docstring to match the problem statement so function names are consistent across problem, template, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution refer to the tensor-network initializer as create_zero_state(num_qubits), but the template repository exposes this entry-point under the different name init_zero_state(num_qubits). This inconsistent identifier for the exact same conceptual entity (creating the MPS zero state) can confuse students when they map the tasks from the problem description to the starter code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function init_zero_state to create_zero_state (and update its docstring and any internal references) so the template API matches the problem statement and the solution implementation. Alternatively, update the problem statement to use init_zero_state consistently, but prefer aligning the template to the problem statement name to match the solution.
